positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Accounting API:
- Worked on an externally-exposed read-only API from beginning to end, involving requirements gathering, design, and frontend and backend work
- Reworked internal accounting system code to be more performant, while also streamlining APIs other services used to interact with it
- After launch, interacted with customers when they needed support using the API or when they had feature requests

Blockchain Governance Voting - Maker governance, Maker polling, Celo governance:
- Worked with external parties to understand how they implemented their voting flows, with vastly different thinking and implementations between different projects
- Communicated clearly with these teams for guidance, as well as providing feedback on their systems, as these projects were often early along in their release cycle
- Designed changes to existing code base to adapt better to the differences between these voting systems; this was a cross-team effort between design, frontend, iOS, and backend teams
- Engineered workarounds for limitations on external data sources, such as flaky APIs, missing data, unstandardized data formats, etc

Reworked User Flow:
- Some parts of the user experience were unintuitive to users, and we wanted to change the app user flow
- Cooperated with the design team and iOS team to determine which improvements were most viable to achieve the best balance between improved UX vs engineering feasibility and commitment
- Led backend engineer team to understand the conceptual shift in code paths and to implement the code changes
- Reviewed future work that would be affected by this large refactor and made sure that other backend engineers were properly informed and assisted in accommodating these changes
- Coordinated heavily with iOS team to ensure that API expectations were set, verifying that API call and user flow were correct, and testing end-to-end before release

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
(Full-Stack) Enterprise Merchant Insights Team

Data Pipeline Automation:

- Issue: daily batch data needed to be processed, old process was manually run by a data scientist
- Evaluated using EMR vs ECS for the Spark cluster, settled on using EMR
- Used AWS Lambda to automate spinning up an EMR cluster and run the necessary Spark job and terminate upon completion


Data Manager:

- Worked on data manager service which monitored and managed our various data stores, such as Elasticsearch, Kafka, and RDS
- Created APIs and UIs to perform basic maintenance functions on Elasticsearch cluster (such as managing snapshots and indices) and RDS (snapshots and editing tables)


Terraform Infrastructure:

- Issue: our team had a microservice architecture using AWS ECS, and at the time refreshing AMIs was a painful process run through our DevOps' command line
- Worked with DevOps to structure Terraform code for ease-of-use and re-use, creating generalized "microservice" modules with variables to be plugged in at runtime
- Created one-click deployment and teardown of microservices by running the Terraform code in Jenkins; added additional code to automatically fill in common variables such as AMI, security groups, etc based on user-provided info such as AWS region
- Created Terraform modules and Jenkins deployment tasks for Elasticsearch, Redis, and RDS


Kafka/Elasticsearch/Data Ingestion Planning:

- Issue: in the case of sudden outages and mandatory AMI refreshes, we needed plans for failures of various components as well as a playbook of how to perform AMI refreshes on our entire architecture
- Helped design plans by pointing out various potential sources of data loss and providing solutions as to how to deal with them; many of my design points were incorporated into our final design

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
(Frontend) Proof of Concept Team

Elasticsearch-based Graph Database and AngularJS Visualizer:

- Graph-based representation of data flows showing upstreams, downstreams, processing jobs involved, and data owners

- Worked on CayleyGraph (https://github.com/cayleygraph/cayley), an open-source graph abstraction layer on top of various existing databases

- Created a visualizer for the data we had had stored in Cayley (similar to Neo4j's graph visualization)

- Created a graph-based query method for our graph database, allowing users to create visually nodes and links with filters on them instead of typing out a Gremlin query. Target audience was business analysts less familiar with more complex text-based query methods.

- Maintained our Elasticsearch cluster, helped upgrade to newer versions when the time came and triaged issues the cluster had.
